raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

LoRA adapter H2D copies in `activate_adapter` sit on the default stream behind whatever compute is still in flight. PCIe DMA and SMs are independent so there's no reason they can't run in parallel.

This adds `--enable-lora-overlap-loading` (off by default). Copies go on a dedicated side stream; the default stream waits on a CUDA event before the next forward pass. Flag off = `nullcontext()`, zero cost.

7 files changed, +275/−13. Core logic is a ~33-line `LoRAOverlapLoader` class (+56/−10 across 5 source files; the remainder is tests).

## Relationship to PR #31941

PR #31941 ("LoRA Per Request Loading Pipelining Support") targets the same general idea but is a different design:

| | This PR | PR #31941 |
|---|---|---|
| **Granularity** | Coarse: entire `activate_adapter` on one side stream, single sync point before next forward | Fine: layer-by-layer pipelining within prefill forward pass, per-layer sync points |
| **Scope** | +56/−10, 5 source files, no forward pass changes | +597/−191, modifies forward pass |
| **When it helps** | Every adapter swap (decode, speculative, any sequence length) | Per-request loading with long inputs (>1000 tokens) |
| **Risk** | Low — flag off is a strict no-op | Higher — invasive changes to forward path |

The two approaches are complementary. This PR is a low-risk, always-on-eligible primitive; #31941 is a more aggressive pipeline for TTFT-critical workloads.

## Not a Duplicate

Searched open PRs for `lora overlap`, `lora stream`, and `activate_adapter stream`. PR #31941 is the closest match but uses a materially different approach (per-layer forward-pass pipelining vs. coarse side-stream with single event). No other open PR addresses the coarse-grained overlap approach implemented here.

## Test Plan

```bash
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_overlap_loader.py -v
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_overlap_loading.py -v
```

**`test_lora_overlap_loader.py`** (unit) — tests `LoRAOverlapLoader` directly:
- `test_synchronize_noop_when_no_pending`: verifies `synchronize()` is safe with no pending event
- `test_correctness_h2d_copy`: 4096×4096 pinned H2D on side stream, checks `torch.equal` against blocking copy
- `test_overlap_produces_matching_results`: side-stream copy overlaps with default-stream compute, asserts compute results match

**`test_lora_overlap_loading.py`** (integration) — 32 layers × rank 64 × hidden 4096 × 4 slots (fp16 pinned), concurrent 4096×4096 matmul on default stream:
- `test_equivalence`: byte-equality (`torch.equal`) between overlap ON and OFF
- `test_timing_overlap_not_slower`: 5-trial mean, overlap must not exceed sequential by >2%

Note: `test_timing_overlap_not_slower` is a performance regression guard; run manually on a GPU node.

## Test Results

Env: 1× H200 80G, CUDA 12.6, PyTorch 2.6, vLLM 0.19.0

```
tests/lora/test_lora_overlap_loader.py:
[PASS] test_synchronize_noop_when_no_pending
[PASS] test_correctness_h2d_copy
[PASS] test_overlap_produces_matching_results

tests/lora/test_lora_overlap_loading.py:
[PASS] test_equivalence: overlap ON/OFF produce identical GPU weights
[INFO] compute only:  10.4 ms
[INFO] H2D only:      6.6 ms
[INFO] sequential:    17.5 ms / iteration
[INFO] overlap:       10.8 ms / iteration
[INFO] speedup:       1.61x
[PASS] test_timing_overlap_not_slower: overlap mode is at least as fast as sequential
```

Overlap time (10.8 ms) is within 4% of compute-only (10.4 ms), meaning H2D is almost fully hidden.

Speedup scales with rank/layers/slots. Never regresses — flag off means no stream, no event, nothing allocated.

Optional sanity: `python examples/offline_inference/multilora_inference.py` with flag on/off, diff output.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request implements asynchronous LoRA weight loading to overlap host-to-device transfers with GPU computation using a side CUDA stream. It introduces the LoRAOverlapLoader class, adds a configuration flag enable_lora_overlap_loading, and includes comprehensive tests for correctness and performance. A critical review comment points out a potential race condition where the side stream could overwrite buffers still in use by the default stream, suggesting a synchronization step and more efficient event handling.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The current implementation is susceptible to a critical race condition. When LoRA slots are reused across iterations, the side stream may start overwriting GPU buffers while the default stream is still executing kernels from the previous iteration that are reading from those same buffers. To ensure correctness, the side stream must synchronize with the default stream before starting the copies. Additionally, creating a new `torch.cuda.Event` on every call is inefficient; using `enable_timing=False` is recommended for synchronization-only events to reduce overhead.

```python
    @contextmanager
    def load_context(self):
        current_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()
        with torch.cuda.stream(self._stream):
            # Ensure we don't overwrite buffers currently in use by the default stream
            self._stream.wait_stream(current_stream)
            yield
        event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=False)
        event.record(self._stream)
        self._pending = event
```

🟡 **Severity: MEDIUM**

The side CUDA stream begins H2D copies without first waiting for the default stream's in-flight work. When a LoRA slot is evicted and reused between consecutive `execute_model` iterations, the side stream can overwrite GPU weight buffers (`lora_a_stacked`/`lora_b_stacked`) while the previous forward pass on the default stream is still reading them, causing a data race on shared GPU memory. A `self._stream.wait_event(default_stream_event)` is needed before entering the side stream context.
Helpful? Add 👍 / 👎

<details>
<summary>💡 Fix Suggestion</summary>

**Suggestion:** Before entering the side CUDA stream context, record an event on the current (default) stream and make the side stream wait on it. This ensures the side stream's H2D copies won't begin until the default stream has finished any in-flight forward-pass kernels that may still be reading the weight buffers.

Add the following before the `with torch.cuda.stream(self._stream):` block:
```python
default_event = torch.cuda.Event()
default_event.record(torch.cuda.current_stream())
self._stream.wait_event(default_event)
```

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.lora.lora_overlap_loader import LoRAOverlapLoader
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required"
+)
+
+
+def test_synchronize_noop_when_no_pending():
+    loader = LoRAOverlapLoader(torch.device("cuda"))
+    assert not loader.has_pending
+    loader.synchronize()
+    assert not loader.has_pending
+
+
+def test_correctness_h2d_copy():
+    loader = LoRAOverlapLoader(torch.device("cuda"))
+
+    cpu = torch.randn(4096, 4096, dtype=torch.float32).pin_memory()
+    gpu = torch.empty(4096, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+
+    with loader.load_context():
+        gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=True)
+
+    assert loader.has_pending
+    loader.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    assert (gpu.cpu() - cpu).abs().max().item() == 0.0
+    assert not loader.has_pending
+
+
+def test_overlap_produces_matching_results():
+    loader = LoRAOverlapLoader(torch.device("cuda"))
+
+    nelem = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+    cpu = torch.randn(nelem, dtype=torch.float32).pin_memory()
+    gpu = torch.empty(nelem, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    work = torch.randn(2048, 2048, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+
+    # warmup
+    for _ in range(10):
+        work = torch.mm(work, work)
+        work = work / (work.abs().max() + 1e-6)
+    gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=False)
+    with loader.load_context():
+        gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=True)
+    loader.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    # overlap: H2D on side stream while compute runs on default stream
+    out_seq = work.clone()
+    for _ in range(400):
+        out_seq = torch.mm(out_seq, out_seq)
+        out_seq = out_seq / (out_seq.abs().max() + 1e-6)
+    gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=False)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    out_ovl = work.clone()
+    for _ in range(400):
+        out_ovl = torch.mm(out_ovl, out_ovl)
+        out_ovl = out_ovl / (out_ovl.abs().max() + 1e-6)
+    with loader.load_context():
+        gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=True)
+    loader.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    assert torch.allclose(out_seq, out_ovl, atol=1e-4)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import time
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.lora.lora_overlap_loader import LoRAOverlapLoader
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required"
+)
+
+# 32 layers × rank 64 × hidden 4096 × 4 slots — mirrors the sglang PR #15512 setup
+N_LAYERS = 32
+RANK = 64
+HIDDEN = 4096
+N_SLOTS = 4
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def weight_buffers():
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    cpu_a = [
+        [torch.randn(RANK, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.float16).pin_memory() for _ in range(N_SLOTS)]
+        for _ in range(N_LAYERS)
+    ]
+    cpu_b = [
+        [torch.randn(HIDDEN, RANK, dtype=torch.float16).pin_memory() for _ in range(N_SLOTS)]
+        for _ in range(N_LAYERS)
+    ]
+    return cpu_a, cpu_b
+
+
+def _make_gpu_buffers(device):
+    gpu_a = [
+        torch.zeros(N_SLOTS, 1, RANK, HIDDEN, device=device, dtype=torch.float16)
+        for _ in range(N_LAYERS)
+    ]
+    gpu_b = [
+        torch.zeros(N_SLOTS, 1, HIDDEN, RANK, device=device, dtype=torch.float16)
+        for _ in range(N_LAYERS)
+    ]
+    return gpu_a, gpu_b
+
+
+def test_equivalence(weight_buffers):
+    """Overlap ON/OFF must produce byte-identical GPU weights."""
+    cpu_a, cpu_b = weight_buffers
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    loader = LoRAOverlapLoader(device)
+
+    gpu_a_seq, gpu_b_seq = _make_gpu_buffers(device)
+    for i in range(N_LAYERS):
+        for s in range(N_SLOTS):
+            gpu_a_seq[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_a[i][s])
+            gpu_b_seq[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_b[i][s])
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    gpu_a_ovl, gpu_b_ovl = _make_gpu_buffers(device)
+    with loader.load_context():
+        for i in range(N_LAYERS):
+            for s in range(N_SLOTS):
+                gpu_a_ovl[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_a[i][s], non_blocking=True)
+                gpu_b_ovl[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_b[i][s], non_blocking=True)
+    loader.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    for i in range(N_LAYERS):
+        assert torch.equal(gpu_a_seq[i], gpu_a_ovl[i]), f"lora_a mismatch at layer {i}"
+        assert torch.equal(gpu_b_seq[i], gpu_b_ovl[i]), f"lora_b mismatch at layer {i}"
+
+
+def test_timing_overlap_not_slower(weight_buffers):
+    """Overlap mode must not be slower than sequential (5-trial mean, 2% margin)."""
+    cpu_a, cpu_b = weight_buffers
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    loader = LoRAOverlapLoader(device)
+
+    gpu_a, gpu_b = _make_gpu_buffers(device)
+    mat_a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)
+    mat_b = torch.randn(4096, 4096, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)
+
+    def model_compute(n_iters=50):
+        x = mat_a
+        for _ in range(n_iters):
+            x = torch.mm(x, mat_b)
+        return x
+
+    def do_copies():
+        for i in range(N_LAYERS):
+            for s in range(N_SLOTS):
+                gpu_a[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_a[i][s], non_blocking=True)
+                gpu_b[i][s, 0].copy_(cpu_b[i][s], non_blocking=True)
+
+    # warmup
+    model_compute(n_iters=5)
+    do_copies()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    with loader.load_context():
+        do_copies()
+    loader.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    n_trials = 5
+
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    for _ in range(n_trials):
+        model_compute()
+        do_copies()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    seq_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / n_trials * 1000
+
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    for _ in range(n_trials):
+        model_compute()
+        with loader.load_context():
+            do_copies()
+        loader.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    ovl_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / n_trials * 1000
+
+    assert ovl_ms <= seq_ms * 1.02, (
+        f"Overlap ({ovl_ms:.1f} ms) slower than sequential ({seq_ms:.1f} ms)"
+    )

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The current implementation is susceptible to a critical race condition. When LoRA slots are reused across iterations, the side stream may start overwriting GPU buffers while the default stream is still executing kernels from the previous iteration that are reading from those same buffers. To ensure correctness, the side stream must synchronize with the default stream before starting the copies. Additionally, creating a new `torch.cuda.Event` on every call is inefficient; using `enable_timing=False` is recommended for synchronization-only events to reduce overhead.

```python
    @contextmanager
    def load_context(self):
        current_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()
        with torch.cuda.stream(self._stream):
            # Ensure we don't overwrite buffers currently in use by the default stream
            self._stream.wait_stream(current_stream)
            yield
        event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=False)
        event.record(self._stream)
        self._pending = event
```

🟡 **Severity: MEDIUM**

The side CUDA stream begins H2D copies without first waiting for the default stream's in-flight work. When a LoRA slot is evicted and reused between consecutive `execute_model` iterations, the side stream can overwrite GPU weight buffers (`lora_a_stacked`/`lora_b_stacked`) while the previous forward pass on the default stream is still reading them, causing a data race on shared GPU memory. A `self._stream.wait_event(default_stream_event)` is needed before entering the side stream context.

<summary>💡 Fix Suggestion</summary>

**Suggestion:** Before entering the side CUDA stream context, record an event on the current (default) stream and make the side stream wait on it. This ensures the side stream's H2D copies won't begin until the default stream has finished any in-flight forward-pass kernels that may still be reading the weight buffers.

## Code Review

This pull request implements asynchronous LoRA weight loading to overlap host-to-device transfers with GPU computation using a side CUDA stream. It introduces the LoRAOverlapLoader class, adds a configuration flag enable_lora_overlap_loading, and includes comprehensive tests for correctness and performance.
